subject: Adaptive savings framework — Optimize toolkit pricing & technical guidance

Subject: Adaptive savings framework — Optimize toolkit pricing & technical guidance

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for taking this — we kicked off an internal initiative to reduce inference spend and your Optimize toolkit was recommended by a colleague. A few quick datapoints on our usage to help your team size potential savings: average request (prompt + completion) ~150 tokens historically, monthly volume ~20M tokens (current), ~60% prefix reuse on conversational flows, peak concurrent requests ~120, and typical p95 latency target for customer-facing flows is ~350ms.

What we're trying to understand: 1) realistic order-of-magnitude cost reductions we should expect from combining prefix/KV caching, continuous batching, and quantization; 2) recommended quantization profile(s) for our workload (we're using Redwood-OG-13B for most flows); and 3) pilot structure / credits needed to validate production rollout.

Can you share a short pilot proposal and an initial savings range (conservative / likely / aggressive)? Attaching a small usage extract. Happy to set a quick 30m to walk through details.

—Alex
Alex Turner
Head of Infrastructure, Finlytics
[Attachment: finlytics_usage_q1.csv]
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finlytics.ai>
Date: 2027-05-19T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Adaptive savings framework — Optimize toolkit pricing & technical guidance

Alex — thanks for the context and the usage extract. High-level we typically see three levers with fairly independent effects:

- Prefix / KV caching: reduces repeated prompt compute and KV cache misses; typical uplift 8–25% depending on chat reuse patterns.
- Batching (continuous + adaptive): reduces per-token overhead, typically 5–15% for interactive workloads; impact increases at higher concurrency.
- Quantization: model-dependent; for 13B-class we recommend q4 profiles for latency-sensitive routes and q8/q5 for throughput-first paths — savings range 12–35% with minor quality tradeoffs.

Conservative combined estimate: ~15% savings. Likely: 22–28%. Aggressive (high cache hit + higher quantization): up to ~40%. These are ballpark until we run a short pilot against your real traffic.

Next steps: please share an hour range when your infra lead can join (we'll include our inference engineer). Connor O'Brien from our commercial team will follow up with pilot options and formal terms.

—Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-05-20T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Adaptive savings framework — Pilot structure & initial econ asks

Alex — looping in a few specifics so we can produce a concrete pilot proposal. Couple of asks that materially affect savings estimates:

1) Request distribution (requests/sec by hour, tail percentiles) — helps size batching windows and expected batch sizes.
2) Typical prefix reuse duration (seconds between repeated prefixes) — drives KV hit curve.
3) Model variant details (you mentioned Redwood-OG-13B; are you on a mixed fleet with a larger model for fallback?).
4) Quality guardrails — acceptable delta (if any) for switching to q4/q8 quant profiles.

Proposed pilot: 2 weeks of live traffic routing through Redwood Optimize with instrumentation + 10M token credit. Deliverables: measured cache hit and effective token reduction, measured batching uplift, cost delta by quant profile, and a short eval report on quality.

Commercial framing (initial): trial credit + a short-term trial discount (we typically offer 10–12% off list for pilots that use our runtime), and a committed band discount table for 12/24 month reserved capacity. We'll put numbers to this once we have the distribution and latency SLO.

If you can share your telemetry (request/sec CSV + a short test token sample), I can draft a pilot term sheet by EOD Friday.

—Connor

Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Alex Turner <alex.turner@finlytics.ai>
Date: 2027-05-20T15:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Adaptive savings framework — technical recs for Finlytics

Alex / team — quick technical recommendation set from the inference side based on the 13B baseline you mentioned. Short version: we can safely pursue an aggressive caching + mixed-quant strategy with low risk to quality if we validate with an eval harness. Details: 

- Quantization: for Redwood-OG-13B we recommend starting with q4_0 on customer-facing, latency-sensitive routes (minimal perceptible quality delta) and q8_0 for internal batch/analytics routes where P50/P95 are less strict. If you need slightly better numeric fidelity on some regressions, q5_0 is a middle path.

- Caching: enable prefix/KV caching with an LRU eviction tuned to your prefix reuse window. With 60% reuse reported, we expect cache hit 40–60% on conversational flows; that translates directly into reduced decoding compute. We'll instrument both 'token avoid' (tokens not processed due to cache) and 'KV hit rate' to attribute savings.

- Batching: we recommend continuous batching with adaptive micro-batching (20–40ms collection window), with a hard max batch size of 64 requests for the pilot. That balances latency and throughput given your 120 peak concurrent requests. If concurrent increases to 180+, raising max batch to 128 improves unit cost.

- Fallbacks: configure a graceful fallback flow that uses a slightly larger model or non-quantized path for requests that fail quality checks. This keeps customer experience intact while letting more traffic use optimized execution.

I'll prepare a small evaluation harness (30–50 prompts) you can run against q4/q8 to surface any failure modes — we typically see <2% user-visible quality regression on chat-style completions for q4 on 13B.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Applied Inference Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Adaptive savings framework — details and next steps

Thanks — this is exactly the level we need. A few clarifications: we're using Redwood-OG-13B across the board with occasional fallback to Redwood-OG-30B for longer-form synthesis (about 15% of requests). Our average observed request size including completion is ~350 tokens (we expect this to rise as features launch), and current monthly volume is nearer 22–25M tokens. Peak concurrency on business hours spikes yesterday to ~180. Our finance team wants a clear SLA for p95 latency (target 400ms) and an outline of the pricing bands for a 6- and 12-month commit.

We're open to the 2-week pilot and the 10M credit — can you put together a concrete pilot term sheet and the evaluation harness you mentioned? Also, if you have prior anonymized case references where caching + quantization achieved >25% net savings on 13B-class models, that would help my CFO.

—Alex
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Pilot proposal & pricing bands — Finlytics (DL-4521)

Alex — attaching a compact pilot proposal and a pricing band snapshot tailored to the usage you described. Highlights: 

- Pilot: 2 weeks live routing with instrumentation + 10M token credit. Deliverables: cache & batching measurement, quantized cost comparators (q4/q8/q5), and a short quality report (we'll run the 50-sample harness Karthik prepares).

- Trial commercial: 10% trial discount applied to billable tokens during the pilot window; no long-term commitment required to run pilot.

- Commit bands (monthly committed token volume):
  * 12-month reserve: 18% off list + reserved capacity SLA (p99 latency uplift guard, dedicated slot priority).
  * 6-month reserve: 12% off list + preferred routing (shared capacity).
  * Flex (no reserve): pay-as-you-go with Optimize toolkit recommendations, pilot credits applied.

- Measurement & governance: instrumentation will report token-level cost, effective token reduction from KV cache, batching uplift, and a quality regression flag (auto-alert to your SRE and ours). SLA for p95 latency at commit stage can be contractually defined; for pilot we baseline performance and propose targets.

Attachments: Optimize_Playbook_Finlytics_v1.pdf (playbook + expected instrumentation points), Finlytics_Pilot_Terms.xlsx (pilot credit & acceptance criteria).

Next steps: if you confirm the pilot window we'll schedule a kickoff call (we recommend including your infra lead and product owner). I'll also include a short anonymized case study showing a 28% net reduction on a 13B-class fleet in a similar chat-use case.

If that works I'll send a formal DocuSign for the pilot terms by tomorrow.

—Monica

Commercial Operations Lead | Redwood Inference
